- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.5) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.5) and forecast is trending downward, reduce downward slope or add mean-reversion bias.  
- If recent history shows sharp spikes followed by rapid drops, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast peak at 1–2% below prior high.  
- If forecast is flat or slowly rising but true outcome shows strong mean reversion, adjust downward by 1–3% in next 5–7 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from forecast mean in first 5–7 days, apply “early correction” by 1–2% downward adjustment.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or neutral sentiment, model tends to drift — apply slight downward bias (0.5–1.5%) to avoid false momentum.  
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust — add a “sentiment pivot” rule: if sentiment >0.3 after day 10, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for remaining days.
